title: AI Cyberattacks Surge to 25% of Global Data Breaches
source_used: Chosun Ilbo (English edition), page text read from the page's embedded article data
key_facts: IBM's '2026 Cost of a Data Breach' report, published in July, covers 602 organizations from March 2025 to February 2026.
25% of malicious breaches used AI-based attacks, up 56% on the year before.
Average damage from AI hacking was about 6 million dollars against 4.99 million dollars for all breaches.
62% of AI-based attacks targeted core infrastructure, mostly finance and energy.
More than 20% of surveyed firms had breaches aimed at AI models or applications.
For 30 South Korean firms, 31% of malicious breaches were AI-driven.
In a May survey of 456 organizations, over half used AI agents to detect attacks but only 18% used them to find and fix weaknesses ahead of time.
quote_evidence: Sixty-two percent of AI-based attacks targeted core infrastructure, with the financial and energy sectors facing the highest concentration of attacks.
only 18% utilized them to proactively identify and fix security vulnerabilities.
why_it_matters_hint: Quantifies AI's share of breaches and a defence gap.
